chapter: Arriving in New York and founding the Afro-Cubans
title: Mario leaves Calloway to join Machito's band
summary: Mario cabled that he was tired of the road, and they agreed to split the expenses; his arranger contacts helped the band.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: All right. In July, I found out, of 1940 Mario Bauza left Calloway and your band was appearing at The Great White Way.
Tell me about that meeting. What happened?

Well, he sent me a cable from Chicago and said, 'Nacho, I am sick and tired to be running all over the country', and so on and so on, 'and wind up with anything because it's too expensive' or whatever, 'so I am going to New York and I am going to join your band and we get together. Don't worry, I rehearse the band and prepare everything', and whatever. I said, no, no, no, no, let's be half and half, we pay all the expenses and we divide whatever. And he said okay, because we was, you know, family.

So that became this new trend because he had a lot of connections with good arrangers like John Bantee and the other guy from Tommy Dorsey, Jimmy Dorsey, everyone because he was the one to give the okay in Chick Webb's band for those arrangements. So he was doing a favor to a lot of guys in that particular, that particular way, so we had a lot of favors from those people. We are very grateful because we don't have no money to pay all those top-flight arrangers.
